children.text: JDPI's Strengthening Protection and GBV Response in Madagali project includes vocational skills training and start-up support to expand livelihood opportunities for young people.

The annual report illustrates this component through barbering training, practical business skills and an equipment kit containing a solar power station, clippers and other tools. Skills and start-up equipment help participants establish small businesses and strengthen their livelihoods.
Source: JDPI Annual Report 2025, page 55. The report does not provide the project's start or end date.

children.text: Under WE-SING, 100 women in Borno State received livelihood start-up kits in 2025. Support was tailored to participants' chosen activities, including tailoring, petty trading and food processing, helping them establish or expand small enterprises.
The annual report also records individual counselling for 30 women under WE-SING. Together, these livelihood and psychosocial activities support women's wellbeing, confidence and economic resilience.
Source: JDPI Annual Report 2025, pages 16 and 31. The report does not provide the project's start or end date.

children.text: The ECHO-funded SAHaRA project provided unrestricted cash assistance to 15,466 individuals across Borno and Adamawa States in 2025. This enabled households to access food and essential supplies according to their own priorities.

The report also attributes 2,675 cholera and hygiene kits and menstrual hygiene kits for 1,115 people to the ECHO Sahara project. These interventions complemented hygiene awareness and cholera prevention work.

Source: JDPI Annual Report 2025, pages 16 and 27. The accompanying photograph illustrates JDPI hygiene promotion from the report's WaSH section; its caption does not identify it as a SAHaRA-specific event. The report does not provide the project's start or end date.

aboutIntro: The Justice Development and Peace Initiative (JDPI) Maiduguri is the development and humanitarian organisation of the Catholic Diocese of Maiduguri, working with vulnerable communities across Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States. children.text: The 2025 annual report highlights community greenhouses established through the BMZ-supported resilience project in Hong and Michika, Adamawa State. Twenty greenhouses supported 263 vulnerable households with opportunities for climate-smart production and stronger livelihoods.
Source: JDPI Annual Report 2025, page 17. These figures describe the report's 2025 greenhouse intervention, not the project's lifetime reach.

activities.title: Post-harvest support

profile.context: Households in Northeast Nigeria face the combined pressures of conflict, displacement, climate variability and limited livelihood opportunities. Dependence on seasonal rain makes production vulnerable to long dry periods. The project links practical support with local skills and community structures to strengthen recovery.

A completed community greenhouse viewed from above

overview: The BMZ-funded Multisectoral Strengthening of Resilience project supports vulnerable households in conflict-affected communities of Northeastern Nigeria and Northern Cameroon. JDPI’s reported work in Hong and Michika combines livelihood recovery with community-led approaches to nutrition, water access and peacebuilding.

In 2025, community greenhouses helped households grow vegetables beyond the rainy season. Alongside agricultural support, the report highlights nutrition learning, income-generating activities and dialogue that strengthen resilience across everyday life.

children.text: Advancing Local Leadership in the Right Way (ALLRight) is an organisational-strengthening project funded by Catholic Relief Services, with technical assistance from CRS. It supports JDPI's systems, leadership, accountability and sustainability so the organisation can deliver stronger community services.

The 2025 report describes the rollout of JDPI's Resource Mobilisation Strategy, helping staff strengthen fundraising and diversify funding opportunities. It also records the development of a comprehensive monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) policy and a five-day policy rollout training for staff.
Source: JDPI Annual Report 2025, page 58. The report does not provide the project's start or end date.

image.alt: JDPI staff and donors at the ALLRight resource mobilisation strategy rollout

activities.text: Rolled out and disseminated JDPI’s Resource Mobilisation Strategy to strengthen fundraising and diversify funding opportunities.
activities.title: Resource mobilisation

activities.text: Developed a comprehensive monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning policy with support from CRS.
activities.title: MEAL policy development

activities.text: Delivered a five-day policy rollout training focused on shared approaches to data collection, analysis, reporting and use.
activities.title: Staff capacity

profile.context: Community impact depends on strong local institutions as well as direct assistance. ALLRight addresses the organisational systems and skills JDPI needs to sustain its work, mobilise resources and make evidence-informed decisions.

overview: Advancing Local Leadership in the Right Way (ALLRight) strengthens JDPI’s organisational systems, leadership, accountability and long-term sustainability. The project is funded by Catholic Relief Services, with technical assistance from CRS.
By investing in the institution behind the programmes, ALLRight supports more effective services and stronger locally led development for the communities JDPI serves.
